participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, runs the meeting)
Andrew Musial (closer, labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' in the transcript)
Richard Claessen (closer, new to the team)
summary: Weekly sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan, roughly 54 minutes. Opens with personal wins, then moves to roster changes — Harry Edmonds, Kyla and Ben Byrne have all left the team, and Richard Claessen has been promoted from overflow cover into a full closer seat. Chris sets a $80,000 upfront-cash month target and walks each rep through weekly projections: Andrew commits to $50,000 for the month and $22,600 this week across the remaining days; Richard commits to four units and $12,000; Kim reports zero units set last week and three sets so far today. The back half is coaching. Chris tells Richard to stop sending payment links and to take card details live on the call instead, role-plays a prospect who wants to pay after the call, and instructs the team never to let a buyer off the phone before payment. He also sets a deposit rule, addresses a broken no-show text workflow that reaches prospects from an unattributed phone number, and closes with a longer piece on self-development as the lever above process once a rep knows the script.
notable: PAYMENT POLICY STATED: deposits are permitted. 'If you do get a deposit from somebody or something, like, if you get a $500 deposit, okay, you can book the onboarding call, but they have to pay at least the $1,200 before the onboarding call happens, and if they don't, cancel it and be on top of it ASAP.' Both figures sit outside the $6,000/$9,000 structure.

PAYMENT-LINK POLICY STATED, and it cuts against the audit's own close rule. Chris: 'stop sending payment links... 99.9% of the time I do it myself.' A payment link is treated internally as a failure mode, not a close step — relevant to any disposition resolved by 'verbal agreement plus link sent'.

Chris coaches reps to keep buyers on the phone through payment: 'I don't let them get off the phone,' and to take card details directly — 'So what card did you want to put that on? Did you want to do MasterCard, Amex, Visa?'

Chris tells reps NOT to run the financial-picture questions unless the prospect volunteers red flags: 'If somebody doesn't give you very clear red flags about finances, you just don't... try to push them onto the prospect.' The playbook's Objection C prescribes a full financial inventory including credit cards and available credit.

Public price signal is known to be wrong and management chose to leave it: 'if somebody types in Trevor Instinct coaching cost, immediately it says $200 a month. Or if you want one-on-one coaching, it's like somewhere between $400 and $700 a month, which is totally wrong... it doesn't really matter if somebody comes in thinking it's a certain price.'

Primal University is $200/month, sold publicly on Skool, and the team is actively considering pulling it off public sale and selling it only on calls. Richard also asks about moving it to '2k payments on school instead of the $200 a month'.

No-show triage automation is misfiring: the third text in the sequence sends from a phone number assigned to nobody, and prospects reply asking who is contacting them. Kim: 'people just respond, saying, like, who is this? Because it gets sent from another phone number.'
Roster churn confirmed — Harry Edmonds, Kyla and Ben Byrne are all off the team as of this date. Ben was exited on performance. This bounds any per-rep comparison across the corpus.
Compensation disclosed: $500 bonus per $50,000 cash collected, recurring payments counted; $1,500/month extra at $150,000 recurring.

Andrew's own projection maths implies an average unit well under list — 13 units for $47,600 is roughly $3,660 per unit, which is consistent with instalments and deposits being routine rather than exceptional.
A $6,000 paid-in-full close by Andrew is confirmed in the opening seconds: 'coming in with a nice little 6K piff.'
Chris explicitly does not want closing at any cost — 'And that doesn't mean you close people who shouldn't be closed' — which sits alongside the pressure coaching rather than replacing it.
Kim's Fathom bot was removed part-way through ('Get Kim's Fathom out of there'), meaning this meeting exists as more than one recording across reps' folders.
